remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was added; the Actor expressly offered none.
The narrower framing avoids the unsupported claim of a confirmed control failure, but it does not itself prove the policy predicate of a material unresolved risk.

From the available summary alone, BPROC-017-D and BPROC-017-E suggest an unresolved issue and a follow-up condition, but do not clearly establish that the issue met the rejection threshold rather than a hold or escalation threshold.
No dated decision record is shown confirming the vendor was rejected specifically because approval conditions were unmet before award.
Evidence access is limited to actor summaries, so wording, timing, and unresolved status at the decision date cannot be independently checked.
BPROC-017-B and BPROC-017-C remain only corroborative context and cannot independently justify rejection under the stated policy.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence. What changed was the framing: the Actor narrowed the rationale from an unsupported theory of proven control failure to a more defensible theory of unmet approval conditions based on an unresolved storage-control inconsistency. That narrowing is important and reduces overclaiming, but it is not the same as satisfying the remaining compliance predicate. Under the policy, rejection must rest on admissible due-diligence evidence showing a material unresolved risk at the time of decision. On the summary available to this role, that materiality showing remains asserted more than demonstrated, and there is still no independently checkable decision record tying the rejection to unmet approval conditions rather than a stronger, unsupported security conclusion. So the position is less problematic than an overbroad rejection rationale, but still suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
